briefs.explicit:
MISSION BRIEF S-014
Units: metres, seconds, kilograms. Time starts at t = 0 when every robot leaves its start location.

Locations (x, y, zone):
- base: (0, 0), outdoor
- north roof: (4, 90), roof
- control room: (7, 135), indoor
- east fence: (82, -118), outdoor
- south yard: (-75, -30), outdoor

Robots:
- G1 (rover): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 2 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 23 kg), camera. Endurance: 4680 s, including the return to its start.
- D1 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 9 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg). Endurance: 1080 s, including the return to its start.
- M1 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 6 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 3360 s, including the return to its start.

Tasks:
- T1: Inspect north roof with a camera. Location: north roof. Duration: 180 s. Needs: camera.
- T2: Inspect north roof with a camera. Location: north roof. Duration: 60 s. Needs: camera. Deadline: finished by t = 300 s.
- T3: Collect a soil sample (2 kg) at east fence and keep it on board. Location: east fence. Duration: 180 s. Needs: robotic arm, cargo carrier (payload 2 kg).
- T4: Photograph control room for the condition report. Location: control room. Duration: 90 s. Needs: camera.
- T5: Collect a soil sample (1 kg) at south yard and keep it on board. Location: south yard. Duration: 60 s. Needs: robotic arm, cargo carrier (payload 1 kg). Deadline: finished by t = 300 s.

Rules:
1. Every task is done by exactly one robot. A robot does its tasks one at a time, in the order you list them, travelling between task locations.
2. A robot can only do a task if it has the needed equipment, enough payload capacity, and can reach the task location.
3. A task that must start after another task waits until that task is finished, even if a different robot does it.
4. Each robot must be back at its start location before its endurance runs out.
5. Every task must be finished by t = 900 s.

Objective: minimise the finish time of the last task (the makespan).
briefs.informal:
Hi team, here is today's job at the site.

Positions are in metres from the base at (0, 0). Drones fly straight and can't go indoors; ground robots follow the road grid (so they travel |dx| + |dy|) and can't get onto roofs. Everyone leaves their start spot at time zero.

Places: north roof (4, 90, a rooftop); control room (7, 135, indoors); east fence (82, -118, outside); south yard (-75, -30, outside).

The fleet: G1 is a rover parked at base that hauls up to 23 kg at 2 m/s and runs for 78 minutes including the drive back. It has a camera. D1 is a quadcopter at base with a camera; it flies at 9 m/s, can lift 2 kg, and its battery lasts 18 minutes including the flight home. M1 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 6 kg, moves at 1.5 m/s and lasts 56 minutes including getting back.

Jobs:
(T1) Get eyes on north roof and check the panels - that takes 3 minutes on site.
(T2) Do a visual check of north roof - that takes 1 minute on site and it has to be finished within the first 5 minutes.
(T3) Pick up a soil sample at east fence and keep it on board; it weighs 2 kg - that takes 3 minutes on site.
(T4) Document control room with pictures - that takes 1.5 minutes on site.
(T5) Pick up a soil sample at south yard and keep it on board; it weighs 1 kg - that takes 1 minute on site and it has to be finished within the first 5 minutes.

Everything has to be wrapped up within 15 minutes of the start, and the sooner the last job finishes, the better. Every robot has to make it back to where it started before its battery runs out.
